In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use-dependent prolongations of VT cycle lengths by the three drugs are similar to the in vitro use-dependent sodium channel blockades by the three drugs.
the use-dependent effect of type I antiarrhythmics on VT cycle length is clinically relevant and can be predicted from their in vitro sodium channel blocking properties.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use-dependent prolongations of the VT cycle lengths by lidocaine and flecainides were statistically significant and the time course of the VT cycle prolongation by flecainide and procainamide were different.
the use-dependent prolongations in VT cycle length observed in humans were similar to their in vitro time constants.
use-dependent sodium channel block is a significant determinant of the clinical effects of type I antiarrhythmics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
use‐dependent prolongation of ventricular tachyarrhythmia cycle length can be a clinically important mechanism of action for antiarrhythmic agents.

the use-dependent prolongations of the VT cycle lengths during treatment with procaina-mide and flecain-ide were statistically significant and clinically relevant (i.e., they were associated with improved hemodynamic tolerance).
the use-dependent slowing in heart rate is an important mechanism for the antiarrhythmic effect of class I drugs in patients.
